opening_message:
Ticket 1: Anita Young (employee ID E001) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E001.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Anita Young (E001) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the Payroll Specialist role owns the Payroll system, the full_time policy permits admin access. Recommend granting admin to Payroll as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E001 as a contractor with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; max for basic-trained contractor is read. Recommend granting read to Payroll (requested admin exceeds max). Note: this conflicts with HR's note claiming full-time status.
reason: Conflicting employee facts exist: HR states E001 is full-time (which would permit admin for a Payroll Specialist owning Payroll), while Security's database states E001 is a contractor with basic security training, which categorically forbids admin and caps access at read. Because the contractor policy absolutely prohibits admin and the Security agent explicitly flags this conflict, the safe, policy-compliant maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds that maximum, so grant read.
